messages.content: Find the least non-negative integer n with n = 17 (mod 101), n = 29 (mod 103) and n = 43 (mod 107). Then compute the sum of the decimal digits of n. Work through the modular arithmetic carefully and check your answer against all three congruences before replying. The final line of your reply must read exactly: n=<value> digits=<sum>

content.text:
**Setup:** The moduli 101, 103 and 107 are pairwise coprime, so the Chinese Remainder Theorem gives a unique solution modulo 101·103·107 = 1,113,121.

**Step 1: combine the first two congruences.**
Write n = 17 + 101k. Then 17 + 101k ≡ 29 (mod 103).
Since 101 ≡ −2 (mod 103), this becomes −2k ≡ 12, so k ≡ −6 ≡ 97 (mod 103).
That gives n = 17 + 101·97 = 9814, so n ≡ 9814 (mod 10403).

**Step 2: bring in the third congruence.**
Write n = 9814 + 10403m. Modulo 107, 9814 ≡ 77 and 10403 ≡ 24.
So 77 + 24m ≡ 43, which gives 24m ≡ −34 ≡ 73 (mod 107).
The inverse of 24 mod 107 is 58, since 24·58 = 1392 = 13·107 + 1.
Then m ≡ 73·58 = 4234 ≡ 61 (mod 107).

So n = 9814 + 10403·61 = 9814 + 634,583 = 644,397.

**Check against all three congruences:**
- 644,397 − 101·6380 = 644,397 − 644,380 = 17 ✓
- 644,397 − 103·6256 = 644,397 − 644,368 = 29 ✓
- 644,397 − 107·6022 = 644,397 − 644,354 = 43 ✓

Since 644,397 < 1,113,121, it is the least non-negative solution.

**Digit sum:** 6 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 9 + 7 = 33

n=644397 digits=33
